reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses precipitation strengthening mechanisms (shearing) in fcc-based HEAs with L12 precipitates, but the hypothesis concerns bcc refractory HEAs (MoNbTaW) and claims effects on thermoelastic properties via lattice vibrations, which are not addressed in the cited passages. The key premises about precipitate formation in refractory HEAs and their influence on thermoelastic behavior lack specific prior support.
premises: Isothermal aging at ~900°C produces uniformly distributed nanoscale coherent precipitates in refractory HEAs like MoNbTaW.
Nanoscale coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion via shearing or Orowan mechanisms.
Precipitate-induced dislocation impedance enhances yield strength and creep resistance.
Nanoscale precipitates modify lattice vibrational characteristics, altering thermoelastic properties (thermal expansion, elastic modulus).
A clear correlation exists between uniform precipitate distribution and enhanced/altered properties.
